You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 54e2fc28d9cf1be7dd2ebe74b20dc20cc2a3e55d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linaro.org>
Date: Wed, 25 Oct 2017 19:25:09 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] spi: sprd: Fix the possible negative value of BIT()

When enabling the ADI hardware channels, if the channel id is 31,
then we will get one negative value -1 for BIT() macro, which will
write incorrect value to register.

Fixes: 7e2903cb91df ("spi: Add ADI driver for Spreadtrum platform")
Reported-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
---
 drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c b/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c
index 6a5ff3003044..5993bdbf79e4 100644
--- a/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c
+++ b/drivers/spi/spi-sprd-adi.c
@@ -303,7 +303,7 @@ static void sprd_adi_hw_init(struct sprd_adi *sadi)
 		writel_relaxed(chn_config, sadi->base +
 			       REG_ADI_CHN_ADDR(chn_id));
 
-		if (chn_id < 31) {
+		if (chn_id < 32) {
 			value = readl_relaxed(sadi->base + REG_ADI_CHN_EN);
 			value |= BIT(chn_id);
 			writel_relaxed(value, sadi->base + REG_ADI_CHN_EN);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the use of the BIT() macro with a channel ID of 31, which resulted in a negative value (-1) being produced. This occurred because the BIT() macro is defined as (1 << n), and when n is 31, it exceeds the maximum value for a signed integer in a 32-bit system, leading to an incorrect value being written to the register. The fix involved changing the condition to allow channel IDs up to 31 (inclusive), thus preventing the negative value from being generated.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the use of the BIT() macro with a channel ID of 31, which resulted in a negative value (-1) being produced. This occurred because the BIT() macro is defined as (1 << n), and when n is 31, it exceeds the maximum value for a signed integer in a 32-bit system, leading to an incorrect value being written to the register. The fix involved changing the condition to allow channel IDs up to 31 (inclusive), thus preventing the negative value from being generated.
